note: Parkstad daily-life feeds. The tool rewrites air, power, maas, sky, roads, rail, notices and news; the run writes flu, noise, woord (Limburgs word of the day, appended), culture (dated local events, confirmed), admin (dated household admin), roda (next fixtures) and shops. Town-centre coordinates only; no address or postcode is stored. strikes: announced or threatened strikes and action days that touch daily life in Parkstad, the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany or French rail links, written by the run; the page shows the next ones and feeds them to the planner. protests: demonstrations announced or notified in the major Dutch, Belgian and NRW cities and in Maastricht, Heerlen, Liège and Aachen, written by the run; nearest first on the page.

flu.t: Week 44 (26 Oct – 1 Nov): 136 per 100,000 people saw a GP with a respiratory infection, a low level; RIVM on 4 Nov: few people with flu, no epidemic, though flu detections are rising from a low base. Since September RIVM and Nivel report all acute respiratory infections, and the 2026–27 thresholds are not yet set, so the old 58 per 100,000 flu line no longer applies. RIVM's 11 Nov update was not yet published at 05:30.

woord.note: Heerlens and Hoensbroeks; the Dutch mooi is rarely heard in dialect

uitspraak.tip: sj is English sh; oe is a long oo as in moon, longer than the Dutch oe in boek

woord.meaning_en: carnival, the Shrovetide season that opens on 11-11
woord.example: Elf-elf: d'r Vasteloavend is weer begonne!
woord.example_en: Eleven-eleven: carnival season has started again!
woord.note: Heerlen spelling, as e-WLD records it for Heerlen and the gemeente uses it; Sittard and Maastricht write Vastelaovend. The example sentence is ours, since the dictionary gives forms, not sentences.

uitspraak.tip: oa is the long open o of English law; stress falls on LOA, and the final d is said as t

woord.note: Heerlens and Hoensbroeks alike: e-WLD records zauwele for both towns and the phrase ’t is an ’t zauwele for Heerlen. The noun is d'r zauwel, a drizzle, and Hoensbroek calls a light shower a zauwelbuuj.
src: e-WLD, begrip motregenen, licht regenen (Heerlen and Hoensbroek: zauwele)

uitspraak.tip: au as in English now; the -ele ending is two light schwa syllables and the stress stays on the first
sj (written sch in the 1914 example) is English sh run straight into the p; the a is short and open, quicker than in German Spaß, and the final s stays sharp

woord.note: Heerlens: e-WLD records sjpas, sjpasz and sjpàs for Heerlen, with sjpàssich (prettig, fun) and sjpàs-máákə (to have fun); its Hoensbroek entry for the same idea gives lôl instead. Borrowed from German Spaß. The example is e-WLD's Heerlen record from 1914, spelled as recorded. On the Elfde van de Elfde the word is in the name of Stichting Sjpas en Cultuur Parkstad, which Heerlen's event calendar lists as organiser of Aod òp Nuj.
src: e-WLD, begrip pret, schik (Heerlen: sjpas, sjpàs; Hoensbroek: lôl)

woord.example: Ich eet gèr eerpel mit gebroone ui.
woord.example_en: I like eating potatoes with fried onion.

uitspraak.tip: Hold the first vowel long, as in Dutch heer, not the short e of English pet, and swallow the ending to a weak -pul; Dutch speakers should drop the d and the long aa of aardappel altogether.

woord.note: e-WLD records ērpǝl for both Heerlen and Hoensbroek; Kerkrade has a variant. The spelling and the example sentence are the Readbook's, as the dictionary gives forms, not sentences.
